text:
zara: hi all, day 1! i'm on a company Windows laptop using WSL2 (Ubuntu). imported the WireGuard profile for split-tunnel. public internet works in Windows, but inside WSL `curl https://s3.vpce.internal` times out and `dig s3.vpce.internal` returns nothing. i can `ssh ubuntu@bastion.redwood` from Windows and from the bastion `curl https://s3.vpce.internal` works. any tips?

mira: welcome @zara! WSL2 networking can be quirky: DNS resolution inside WSL often uses /etc/resolv.conf which is populated from Windows. first quick check: run `cat /etc/resolv.conf` inside WSL and `ipconfig /all` in Windows to see if the tunnel resolver is present.

zara: inside WSL `/etc/resolv.conf` has 172.22.112.1 (Windows VM NAT). Windows `ipconfig` shows the WireGuard adapter with DNS 10.30.0.2 but not propagated to WSL.

samir: yep that's expected. the WireGuard resolver is on the Windows side but WSL's resolv.conf uses the host's virtual NAT IP. two practical workarounds: 1) update WSL resolv.conf to point directly to the tunnel resolver (sudo rm /etc/resolv.conf; create /etc/resolv.conf with `nameserver 10.30.0.2` and disable auto-generation), or 2) use an SSH tunnel from Windows host to the bastion and then access forwarded ports from WSL via localhost.

zara: is editing /etc/resolv.conf safe? will it persist across reboots?

mira: you need to disable WSL auto-generation: `sudo sh -c 'echo "[network]\ngenerateResolvConf = false" > /etc/wsl.conf'` (actually in /etc/wsl.conf in Windows distribution) and then write your resolv.conf. be careful: Windows updates or restarting WSL may overwrite if not correctly set. alternative is to set `nameserver 10.30.0.2` and add `search vpce.internal` so internal names resolve.

zara: i tried the resolv.conf edit and `dig +short s3.vpce.internal` now returns 10.40.12.33 inside WSL. but `aws s3 ls` still fails with TLS host name mismatch (SAN issue) when i call endpoint by IP.

samir: the TLS mismatch is because the cert expects s3.vpce.internal. once DNS resolves properly it should be OK. after you update resolv.conf, retry `aws s3 ls --endpoint https://s3.vpce.internal`. if the client still uses Windows credentials or proxy settings, you may need to set AWS env vars in WSL too.

zara: good point. also curious: i use Docker inside WSL and builds need to pull from the private S3-backed registry. will fixing resolv.conf fix Docker Desktop behavior?

mira: Docker Desktop inside WSL uses a separate network stack; sometimes it inherits Windows DNS. If Docker can't reach internal endpoints, you can either: 1) configure Docker daemon to use 10.30.0.2 as DNS (daemon.json), or 2) create an SSH tunnel and expose the service on localhost for the Docker build. For builds, many folks use `--build-arg REGISTRY=localhost:5000` with an SSH LocalForward to avoid changing daemon config.

netops: adding that WSL is a common edge-case for our split-DNS rollout. long-term we'll publish a small installer that adjusts WSL config safely and pushes resolver settings for corporate machines. for now, please use the resolv.conf change or SSH tunnels.

zara: thanks, resolv.conf trick fixed DNS. one more oddity: when i run `kubectl port-forward svc/artifacts 8080:80` from my laptop (Windows) and then `curl http://localhost:8080` in WSL, it times out. doing the curl in Windows works. any ideas?

samir: WSL2 localhost forwarding to Windows is generally supported but sometimes the loopback binding differs. `kubectl port-forward` binds to 127.0.0.1 on Windows and WSL can access it via the special host IP (usually the Windows host IP). try `curl http://$(cat /etc/resolv.conf | grep nameserver | awk '{print $2}'):8080` or from WSL use the Windows host IP `curl http://$(grep -m1 nameserver /etc/resolv.conf | awk '{print $2}'):8080`. Alternatively run `kubectl port-forward` inside WSL to avoid cross-network issues.

zara: running the port-forward inside WSL worked. thanks. last question: is the right long-term fix for new hires to avoid manual resolv.conf edits?

mira: yes, netops will push a profile that includes the VPC resolver IP and we'll update the onboarding docs with a WSL section. i'm creating a ticket.

it-bot: created ticket #12005: "WSL2: document and automate WireGuard resolver propagation for new hires (s3.vpce.internal)" assigned to @netops. ETA 2 business days.

zara: awesome, thanks everyone 60a this got me unblocked for the day. appreciate the warm welcome!

netops: feel free to ping if you want to be a test case for the WSL installer. happy to help.
